cleaning_prompt: Clean the current month's U.S. retail broiler composite news text only. Each row corresponds to one calendar month; do not apply global year filters (e.g., 2020+ only). Do not copy recent data (e.g., 2024 BLS/EIA) into older rows. Never invent numbers or infer causality. Focus strictly on U.S. retail price drivers with event/release dates within ±1 year of the row’s year (prefer ±3 months). Drop all off-year data (≥2 years difference), even if embedded in a paragraph with on-year U.S. broiler facts—strip the noise, keep the relevant driver. Preserve only: U.S. feed costs (corn/soy), placements, slaughter, cold storage, export volumes, avian disease (e.g., HPAI), regional weather, retail/wholesale prices, spreads, and demand drivers (e.g., consumer spending, chicken substitution). Exclude: non-U.S. data (e.g., EU, South Korea), non-retail poultry (e.g., eggs), farm practices, company ads, speculative claims, non-chicken proteins, vague sources (e.g., wattagnet.com), and off-topic context. Do not emit empty section headers. Output only when facts remain. One bullet = one clear, quantitative, or directional fact. Tag geography (U.S. / state) and date when present. If supply↑ and demand↓ appear together, keep both. Max ~16 bullets. Do not end mid-sentence. Never delete a usable on-year U.S. broiler price driver just because the paragraph also contains off-year noise. Empty output only if no usable on-period U.S. broiler drivers remain after filtering. Panel safety: each row is one calendar month; clean only that month’s input. No global year cutoffs. No date stuffing. No empty section shells. Date alignment: keep only facts with release dates within ±1 year of the row’s year (prefer ±3 months).
